question: Should OpenClaw accept the legacy Installed Apps opt-in reset and ship this Google Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout after the release-ref ordering is fixed?
rationale: The Android consent gate is focused and privacy-protective, but disabling prior opt-ins and changing Google Play release operations are release and compatibility choices that automation should not decide.

options.title: Fix ordering and approve rollout
options.body: Fix the Data Safety failure window, refresh the branch, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, and land the PR with the legacy opt-in reset.

options.title: Revise disclosure or release lane
options.body: Request wording, consent-version, or release-lane changes if Play review or product policy needs a different prominent-disclosure shape.

options.title: Hold for release materials
options.body: Keep the PR open but unmerged until the external Play Console, privacy policy, and review artifacts are ready to ship together.

recommendation.title: Fix ordering and approve rollout
recommendation.body: Fix the Data Safety failure window, refresh the branch, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, and land the PR with the legacy opt-in reset.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Android settings and Android release-lane history makes this the best available owner for the rollout and conflict-refresh decision.
